guided_chapters.title: Meet titin in the sarcomere
guided_chapters.lay_summary: Titin is one continuous giant protein running from the Z-disc toward the sarcomere center. Here it is shown in red beside actin and myosin so its full half-sarcomere route stays visible.
guided_chapters.expert_expansion: The continuous axial topology and domain order are constrained, while the smooth three-dimensional backbone path remains a schematic presentation of unresolved transverse placement.
not_claimed: a resolved atom-by-atom path
known transverse azimuth along the entire chain

guided_chapters.title: Read its architecture
guided_chapters.lay_summary: Titin is not one uniform coil. Folded Ig and Fn3 domains alternate with disordered segments, and the order of those regions is fixed by the sequence: elastic parts near the Z-disc, anchored scaffold further in.
guided_chapters.expert_expansion: Domain identity and order follow Q8WZ42; instanced archetypes encode class, position, and orientation rather than unique molecular surfaces. The smooth linkers between them are presentation proxies for unresolved conformations.
not_claimed: atom-resolved surfaces for every domain
a known azimuth for every folded domain
that domain spacing is measured everywhere along the molecule

guided_chapters.title: Different regions extend differently
guided_chapters.lay_summary: Stretch does not scale every part of titin equally. Folded Ig chains mainly straighten, while disordered spring regions such as PEVK take a larger share of extension in the force-balanced model.
guided_chapters.expert_expansion: Regional nanometer partitions are modeled by a common-force series-chain solver using sourced force-extension laws; the interpolation is explanatory geometry, not a measured time trajectory.
not_claimed: uniform scaling of titin regions
widespread physiological Ig-domain unfolding
a measured molecular trajectory

guided_chapters.title: Inspect its anchors
guided_chapters.lay_summary: A spring only works if both ends are held. At the Z-disc, two titin N-termini from neighbouring half-sarcomeres clamp a telethonin molecule between them, which is how tension passes across the sarcomere boundary.
guided_chapters.expert_expansion: The antiparallel two-titin-to-one-telethonin topology is structure-supported; the displayed span and the surrounding network are schematic. At the far end titin's C-terminus integrates with the M-band, where the opposing half-sarcomere's titin arrives — reachable from the M-band close-up in Evidence mode.
not_claimed: a resolved complete lateral route for titin through the Z-disc
single-ended telethonin binding
a measured display length for the sandwich glyph

guided_chapters.title: See titin as a scaffold
guided_chapters.lay_summary: Titin changes role along its length. Its I-band regions form the extensible spring, while an eleven-domain super-repeat binds the thick filament: that A-band segment keeps a constant span and organizes the filament rather than stretching.
guided_chapters.expert_expansion: Eleven Ig/Fn3 domains repeat every 45.5 nm along the bound segment, near-commensurate with the 43.1 nm myosin repeat; the 2.4 nm residual is not an exact register. The A-band span is invariant with sarcomere length here, which is what makes the scaffold role legible beside the I-band spring. Titin is widely discussed as a thick-filament ruler and regulator, but this model encodes the geometric scaffold only, never a causal mechanism. The same C-zone carries MyBP-C, an accessory thick-filament protein that is not part of titin; its optional schematic context layer can be switched on here in Evidence mode.
not_claimed: one elastic constant for the whole molecule
atom-level region surfaces
an exact universal A-band azimuth
exact register between the titin super-repeat and the myosin repeat
a settled causal mechanism by which titin sets thick-filament length or regulates myosin

guided_chapters.title: Audit the evidence
guided_chapters.lay_summary: Not every line here is equally certain. Lengths and periodicities are measured, regional extension is solved from a model, and smooth three-dimensional paths are schematic. Every object on screen says which it is.
guided_chapters.expert_expansion: Six evidence classes run from MEASURED to UNKNOWN and are never silently promoted. Click any structure for its claim class, render class, scope, sources, and explicit non-claims; the Evidence drawer groups every claim in the current scene by class.

guided_chapters.lay_summary: This is not an illustration drawn to look convincing. Every shape traces back through counted, inspectable records: cited papers, sourced measurements, evidence-classified data, an executable model, and tests built to reject it.

expert_cards.title: Spring and scaffold: what the A-band super-repeat does and does not settle
expert_cards.body: The A-band segment binds the thick filament through an eleven-domain super-repeat of 45.5 nm axial periodicity, eleven of which lie in the C-zone. In this model its end-to-end span stays constant while sarcomere length changes, so the same molecule reads as an extensible I-band spring in series with a positionally anchored A-band scaffold. That organizing role is what supports describing titin as a molecular ruler for thick-filament assembly, and as a participant in myosin regulation. Both remain active proposals in the literature: the visualization shows the geometric scaffold that motivates them and encodes no causal mechanism, no length-setting rule, and no activation coupling.
not_claimed: a settled ruler mechanism for thick-filament length
a settled regulatory pathway from titin to myosin
exact register between the 45.5 nm titin super-repeat and the 43.1 nm myosin repeat
an exact universal A-band azimuth for the bound segment

findings.text: An eleven-domain super-repeat of 45.5 nm axial periodicity binds the thick filament, with eleven copies in the C-zone.
In this model the bound segment's end-to-end span stays constant while sarcomere length changes.
That titin acts as a molecular ruler setting thick-filament length.
That titin participates causally in myosin regulation.

expert_cards.title: Optional MyBP-C context, and why cardiac coordinates were not imported
expert_cards.body: MyBP-C is an accessory C-zone protein of the thick filament, not part of titin. Fast skeletal muscle evidence supports its presence in the C-zone at the approximately 43 nm repeat, with roughly three molecules per repeat, so the optional layer draws that many sparse markers and nothing more. High-resolution coordinates for MyBP-C exist, but they come from cardiac thick-filament reconstructions. This model's declared scope is human skeletal N2A-containing titin, and adopting a cardiac accessory protein's placement would silently mix isoforms — exactly the error this project's evidence classes exist to prevent. The stripe register, azimuth, reach, and pose therefore stay SCHEMATIC, no molecule is drawn reaching a thin filament, and no titin contact is depicted.
not_claimed: cardiac cMyBP-C coordinates in the skeletal reference model
a universal rigid thick-to-thin bridge
a direct titin–MyBP-C contact
three exact molecules at every human titin super-repeat

findings.text: Fast skeletal MyBP-C occupies the C-zone at the approximately 43 nm thick-filament repeat, at roughly three molecules per repeat.

expert_cards.title: N2A as a mechanical and interaction hub
expert_cards.body: The N2A element is more than a length of spring. It contains a structured UN2A core with flexible flanks, and it binds CARP, which makes it a plausible meeting point between mechanical state and signalling. The visualization keeps N2A as a region of titin and adds no partner molecules: naming a binding event is not the same as resolving where the partner sits in an intact sarcomere.

findings.text: N2A contains a structured UN2A core with flexible flanking sequence.
CARP binding to N2A is experimentally characterised.
That N2A acts as an in-situ signalling hub coupling strain to downstream pathways.
The complete composition and geometry of any N2A signalosome in an intact sarcomere.

expert_cards.title: Titin kinase: an established domain, an unsettled mechanism
expert_cards.body: Titin carries a kinase domain near the A-band/M-band junction. Its presence and its isolated structure are established, and the domain proxy you can see is measured from deposited coordinates. What is not settled is the mechanism: proposals that stretch opens the domain and switches on signalling remain under active debate, so the visualization shows the domain and refuses to animate an activation switch.

findings.text: A kinase domain sits near the A-band/M-band junction of titin.
Isolated kinase-domain structures give the measured proxy dimensions drawn here.
That mechanical strain opens the domain and triggers a specific signalling cascade.
The domain's orientation and conformation inside an intact sarcomere.

not_claimed: a settled mechanosensor mechanism

expert_cards.title: Length-dependent activation: a proposal, not a simulation
expert_cards.body: Muscle produces more force at longer lengths for a given calcium level, and passive titin tension and MyBP-C are among the contributors proposed to explain it. That is a live hypothesis about how a passive spring might bias myosin's regulatory state. This model does not implement it: sarcomere length and biochemical activation remain independent axes here, and no state variable couples one to the other.

findings.text: Force at a given calcium level depends on sarcomere length.
That passive titin tension contributes causally to that length dependence.
That MyBP-C mediates part of the same thick-filament regulation.
Whether this model could distinguish those proposals; it contains no activation solver.

not_claimed: settled causality
that titin is the actomyosin motor

expert_cards.title: One gene, many titins — and one of them is modelled here
expert_cards.body: A single TTN gene produces many titin isoforms through alternative splicing, and different muscles and tissues express different ones. Isoform choice changes the length and composition of the elastic I-band segment, and therefore passive stiffness. This visualization models the canonical human skeletal N2A-containing reference and deliberately adds no second isoform: naming the reference is what keeps a general titin story from becoming a claim about an isoform-neutral molecule.

findings.text: Alternative splicing of one TTN gene yields tissue- and muscle-specific titin isoforms.
This model is the canonical human skeletal N2A-containing reference, Q8WZ42.
How the geometry shown here would differ for another isoform; no second isoform is modelled.

expert_cards.title: What this model still cannot tell you
expert_cards.body: Three gaps are worth naming plainly. The azimuthal arrangement of titin strands around a thick filament is resolved in cardiac muscle but not adopted here, because this model's scope is skeletal. M-band organization is only partly resolved, so the centre is a coordinate reference with sparse schematic crosslinks rather than a structure. And active mechanics are absent entirely: the lattice comparison is a quasi-static length sweep, not a time-resolved contraction.

findings.text: The azimuthal placement of titin strands on a skeletal thick filament; the cardiac arrangement is measured but out of scope.
The molecular organization of the M-band; no M1 density is inferred from the retained averaged maps.
Time-resolved active mechanics, including the real time-varying Poisson ratio of the lattice.

not_claimed: a resolved skeletal titin azimuth
a complete M-band molecular structure
time-resolved active contraction
that these gaps are the only ones
